JUDGMENT .

The Appellant, being aggrieved by the Judgment and Award dated 22/4/2013 passed by the learned Civil Judge Senior Division, Amravati in 2/12 Judg.fa.125.2017.odt Land Acquisition Case No. 191/2007, preferred the present Appeal for enhancement of compensation.

sentences.text: 1 2 . In the present Appeal, the State Government, by its Notification under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (for short, 'the Act of 1894') dated 5/10/2000 for the submergence area of Bembla Project, acquired the land owned by the Appellant bearing field Survey No. 28/3, Gat No. 58 of village Yerad (Bazar), Tahsil Chandur Railway, District Amravati.

According to the Appellant,
after issuing the Notification under Section 4 of the Act of 1894, Notification under Section 6 of the Act of 1894 was published on 31/1/2002.
By final Award dated 14/5/2004, the Land Acquisition Officer has awarded the compensation for cultivable land admeasuring 1 H. 61 R. at the rate of Rs.88036/- per hectare.
As such, the total compensation of Rs.2,33,867/- was paid to the Appellant for acquired land.
According to the Appellant, compensation was not paid as per the prevailing market value and the quality and fertility of land was not properly considered.

She, therefore,
preferred reference for enhancement of compensation before the Civil Judge Senior Division,
Amravati.

3. The learned Reference Court, by the impugned Judgment, 3/12 Judg.fa.125.2017.odt enhanced the compensation of the land owned by the Appellant at the rate of Rs.1,10,000/- per hectare by deducting the amount received by the Appellant.

4. In the instant Appeal, the Appellant claimed enhancement of compensation at the rate of Rs.7,70,000/- along with statutory benefits of 3% solatium, 12% additional value, interest and all other benefits as per the provisions of the Act of 1894.
5. The learned AGP for State and the learned Counsel for Acquiring Body strongly opposed the Appeal.

It is their contention that the Reference Court has awarded enhanced compensation in favour of the Appellant by relying upon the Judgment in identical case bearing LAC No. 288/2006 (Pandurang Wamanrao Solanke V/s State of Maharashtra & Ors.) decided by the Reference Court.

entities.text: Pandurang Wamanrao Solanke V/s State of Maharashtra & Ors.)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Considering the valuation done by the Reference Court, it is clear that there is a proper consideration of all material factors involved in the matter, and hence, there is no need of any interference of this Court in the matter.
6. I have heard learned Counsel for both sides at length and perused the record as well as case laws cited by the Appellant in the matter.

7. The Appellant has pointed out from record the 7/12 extract of the 4/12 Judg.fa.125.2017.odt land,
sale deeds of nearby villages, namely, Khadpa, Hadpa, Ghuikhed, Rustampur and Dabha.
The Appellant further stated that she has examined the Valuer in the matter.
Hence, considering all these documents, which were available before the Reference Court, she is entitled for the compensation at least at the rate of Rs.1,35,000/- per hectare in the matter.

8. The Appellant has relied upon the Judgment of this Court in First Appeal No. 557/2007 (Murlidhar s/o Bapurao Dehanikar V/s The Executive Engineer, Bembla Project, Yavatmal & Ors.)
along with connected Appeals dated 10/7/2012.

entities.text: Bapurao Dehanikar V/s The Executive Engineer, Bembla Project, Yavatmal
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the said Judgment, the land involved was of village Dabha, Tahsil Babhulgaon, District Yavatmal.

It is pointed out by the Appellant that the lands involved in the said Appeals were acquired to implement Bembla Medium Irrigation Project,
more particularly, for submergence the huge lands admeasuring about 10100 hectares of villages Sau.

2 Dabha, Yerad, Kopra, Kolhi etc.
9.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is further pointed out from the same Judgment that this Court has relied upon the policy decision taken by the Water Conservation Department dated 2/6/2010, whereby it was declared that the land acquired for Bembla Project should be paid the compensation at the rate of Rs.1,25,000/- per hectare.

Accordingly, this Court, considering the fact that 5/12 Judg.fa.125.2017.odt there are similarities in respect of agro-climatic condition, crop pattern,
average yield per year, availability of the market and the price for the agricultural produce in Vidarbha region, has held that the lands which are situated at village Dabha, are entitled for the compensation of Rs.1,37,000/- per hectare with all statutory benefits.

10. The Appellant has then relied upon the Judgment of this Court in First Appeal No. 479/2007 (Smt. Kamlabai Rambhau Thakre & Ors. V/s The State of Maharashtra & Ors.) along with other connected Appeals dated 18/1/2013, wherein also this Court considered the acquisition of land for Bembla Project of village Dabha.

entities.text: Kamlabai Rambhau Thakre & Ors. V/s The State of Maharashtra & Ors.)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In this Judgment, this Court, by relying upon the earlier Judgment in First Appeal No. 557/2007 has awarded the compensation at the rate of Rs.1,37,000/- per hectare.

Hence, it is the submission of the Appellant that considering the land of adjoining village i.e. Dabha, the quality of the land and other factors being identical, she is also entitled for the compensation of land at the rate of Rs.1,37,000/- per hectare.
11. The learned Counsel for Respondent/Acquiring Body has strongly objected the submissions of the Appellant.
It is his submission that Village Dabha is a big village than the village Yerad (Bazaar).
Hence, considering the population and other facilities at village Dabha, this Court has awarded the 6/12 Judg.fa.125.2017.odt compensation at the rate of Rs.1,37,000/- per hectare.
However, the same factors are not applicable in the case of Appellant being a small village and same is near about a distance of 5 to 6 kms. from the village Dabha.

The price, which is made applicable at village Dabha,
cannot be made applicable for the village Yerad (Bazar).

12. The learned Counsel for Respondent/Acquiring Body has pointed out that the Reference Court,
by relying upon the Judgment passed in the Land Acquisition Case No. 288/2006, wherein by doing all the possible calculations, enhanced the compensation upto Rs.1,10,000/- per hectare.

Hence,
same is required to be applied in the present matter.
13. In view of rival submissions made by leaned Counsel for both the parties, firstly I have gone through the Land Acquisition Case No. 288/2006, which is relied upon by the Reference Court.

From the findings of the Reference Court in LAC No. 288/2006, it is clear that the Reference Court,
on the basis of guesswork reached to the conclusion that the land owner of village Yerad are entitled for compensation at the rate of Rs.1,10,000/- per hectare.

Hence, the decision taken on a guesswork,
according to me, cannot be said to be binding factor in the matter.

In the present matter, the Appellant has led evidence through the Power of Attorney holder namely, Shantaram Vishwanathji Jawalkar before the Reference Court to prove that the quality of Sau. Nirmala Shantaram Jawalkar vs State Of Maharashtra, Through ...

land, the yield, which he has taken from the field and his income from the field, which according to him, was Rs.1,30,000/-.
Hence, he is entitled for the compensation of Rs.1,30,000/- per hectare along with other statutory benefits.

This witness was cross-examined by the Respondents, however,
the statement of this witness was not shaken in the cross-examination and he seems to be consistent on his statement.
As such, nothing contradictory was brought on record in the cross-examination of the Appellant.

15. The Appellant, in support of her claim, examined the Government Authorised Valuer namely,
Balu Shankarrao Vaidya.

He has categorically stated in his evidence that by applying the inflation index as per the Rules he has done detail study, and accordingly, on the basis of considering the valuation of the land amount was determined by him.
He further stated that he has personally visited the agricultural field, took photographs and same are annexed with his report.

Hence,
according to him, he has considered the total valuation of the land admeasuring 1 H. 61 R. as Rs.9,81,000/-.
16.
This witness was also cross-examined by the Respondents.
In the 8/12 Judg.fa.125.2017.odt cross-examination it is brought on record that he has not looked into any sale deed of village Yerad.
It is also brought on record that the land, which is acquired, is only admeasuring 0.23 R. land and it is not affordable for the agriculturist to cultivate such small piece of land.
But nothing is come on record that the valuation was not in proper manner or he was not authorised Valuer etc.
17. According to the Appellant, in view of this evidence placed on record, it is clear that the Government Valuer has expressed the entire things, which normally authorised Valuer done in the matter.
Therefore, it is clear that considering the land of adjoining village Dabha, he is entitled for the compensation, which was given to the similarly situated agriculturist of village Dabha.

18. The Appellant, in support of her submission, has relied upon the Judgment of this Court in the case of Thakarsibhai Devjibhai and Others V/s Executive Engineer, Gujarat and Another along with other connected Appeals, (2001) 9

entities.text: Thakarsibhai Devjibhai and Others V/s Executive Engineer, Gujarat and Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Supreme Court Cases 584, wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that if the distance between the lands under acquisition and the land which is acquired is only about 5 kms, then in such cases if the land is of similar quality, including potentiality, and other factors, then the distance 9/12 Judg.fa.125.2017.odt between two lands would not by itself lead to change their respective market value.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court has observed in paragraph No.12 of the said Judgment as under :
"12.
As we have said above the High Court fell into error by reducing the quantum of compensation on this basis.
The reduction has been made for two reasons, one, that the present acquisition is of larger area and second, the distance between the land under acquisition and in Exh. 16 is about 5 km.

With reference to question of acquisition being of a larger area, the error is, when we scan we find for the acquisition of each landowner, it could not be said that the acquisition is of a large area.
Largeness is merely when each landholder's land is clubbed together then the area becomes large.
Each landowner's holdings are of small area.

Even otherwise,
visioning in line with the submission for the State we find Exh.16 is about two Sau.

4 hectares of land which cannot be said to be of a small piece of land.

entities.text: Nirmala Shantaram Jawalkar vs State Of Maharashtra
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: So far as the other question of distance between the two classes of lands is concerned, that by itself cannot derogate the claim of the claimant unless there are some such other materials to show that quality and potentiality of such land is inferior.

However, distance between the land under Exh.16 and the present land, even if they are 5 km apart,
would not be relevant, the relevancy could be, their distances from Viramgam town.
We find, as per the map produced by the State, the present acquired land is about 3 km away from it, while the land under Exh.16 is about 2 km away from it.
This difference is not such as to lead to reduce the rate of compensation, specially on the facts of this case.
In the present case, as we have recorded above, it has been found that the quality including potentiality of land between Ext.16 and the present one are similar.
No evidence has been led on behalf of the State to find any difference between the two.

In view of this, the inference drawn 10/12 Judg.fa.125.2017.odt by the High Court for reducing the compensation by Rs.10 per sq. M cannot be sustained."
19.

In the light of above submission and the specific evidence brought on record of the adjoining village, I am of the opinion that considering the evidence, which is placed on record, it is clear that the prevalent market value of the land in these villages are identical to that of Appellant's land.

Same instances certainly establishes the actual market value prevalent on the date of publication of Notification under section 4 of the Act of 1894.
20.

The reliance placed by the learned Reference Court while granting compensation at the rate of Rs.1,10,000/-, according to me, is on the basis of guesswork and not without considering the prevalent market value of the land.
It is clear from the record that the land of the Appellant and the land of the villagers of adjoining village was acquired for the same purpose i.e, for submergence of Bembla Project.
The Respondent/Acquiring Body failed to bring on record any evidence that the quality and fertility of the land owned by the Appellant is not same to the land of adjoining village.
Therefore, in absence of such evidence, the statement of the Respondent cannot be accepted.

21. As already stated above, this Court, in the case of Murlidhar Bapurao Dehanikar V/s Executive Engineer & Ors. in First Appeal No. 11/12 Judg.fa.125.2017.odt 557/2007 has recorded the finding that Water Conservation Department itself has declared the compensation for the lands acquired for Bembla Project should be paid at the rate of Rs.1,25,000/- per hectare.

entities.text: Murlidhar Bapurao Dehanikar V/s Executive Engineer & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the said Judgment there is a reference of village Yerad (Bazar) also.

This Court, by considering the fact of agro-climatic condition, crop pattern, average yield per year, availability of market and price for the agricultural produce, enhanced the compensation at the rate of Rs.1,37,000/- per hectare.
Hence, I am of the opinion that considering the distance between the village Dabha and Yerad is merely 4 to 5 kms, the Appellant is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,30,000/- per hectare.

22. The Appellant further prayed for escalation interest at the rate of 10% per annum, by considering the fact that the land, which was acquired at Dabha, has been awarded compensation at the rate of Rs.1,30,000/-, which was under the Notification dated 2/3/2000.
The land of the Appellant was acquired for the same project by the Notification dated 5/10/2000.

Hence,

5 considering the period of seven months, according to me, she is entitled of Rs.700/- towards escalation interest.
Hence, the Appellant is entitled for total enhanced compensation at the rate of Rs.1,30,700/- [Rs.1,30,000/- + Rs.700/- = Rs.1,30,700/-] per hectare.
In the result, following order is passed.
12/12 Judg.f  ORDER  1.
First Appeal is allowed.

2. The Appellant is entitled to get enhanced compensation at the rate of Rs.1,30,700/- per hectare for the land admeasuring 1 H. 61 R., Survey No. 28/3, Gat No. 58 of village Yerad (Bazar), Tahsil Chandur Railway, District Amravati, by deducting the amount, which was already received by the Appellant.
3. Respondents are directed to deposit the enhanced amount either before Reference Court or before this Court within a period of three months with due intimation to Appellant.
4. Rest of the order of Reference Court is confirmed.
5. No order as to costs.
